comedic_beats.description: Husband notices a couple holding hands for three blocks and asks his wife why they don't do that anymore.
comedic_beats.why_it_lands: The droopy, half-lidded 'low battery' character design (visible in scene-0.jpg/periodic-2.jpg) sells the observation as weary rather than accusatory, so the line reads as a tired, universal long-relationship gripe instead of a fight-starter.

comedic_beats.description: Wife's deflecting non-answer 'We do other things' is met with a 0.58s pause, then his flat challenge 'Like what?' after another 0.56s pause.
comedic_beats.why_it_lands: Two back-to-back sub-second silences (0.577s and 0.5605s per silence_pauses.json) around a vague deflection mimic the real stalling beat of a couple who both already suspect there's no good answer coming.

comedic_beats.description: She answers the challenge by reframing tolerating his snoring and duvet-stealing as their version of romance: 'I let you snore and steal the duvet every night.'
comedic_beats.why_it_lands: The line is delivered with the same flat, slightly smiling mouth shape as periodic-8.jpg ('STEAL') rather than any hurt or humor cue, so the substitution of grievance for affection lands as sincere logic instead of a bit, which is what makes it funny.

comedic_beats.description: After the longest pause in the whole clip (0.909s, per silence_pauses.json), she caps the reframe with a dismissive, absolute verdict: 'Holding hands is nothing.'
comedic_beats.why_it_lands: The 0.909s hang is nearly double any other gap in the transcript, giving her crossed-arms, chin-up certainty (periodic-10.jpg) time to register before the flat dismissal, turning a marital deflection into a confidently deranged thesis statement.

comedic_beats.description: sight-gag: both characters are built with permanently sagging, tired 'melted' faces and slumped posture throughout the entire exchange, regardless of what they're saying.
comedic_beats.why_it_lands: The visual joke of the show's premise (title cards literally say 'Low Battery People') runs underneath the dialogue the whole scene: even at her most confidently absurd, her eyelids stay half-closed and her posture stays deflated, so the exhaustion never breaks character to punctuate any single line -- it's the constant backdrop the marital bit is staged against.

overall_comedic_style_notes: The whole beat is a single unbroken two-shot conversation (0-11.63s, one scene) with no cutaways, so all the comedy is carried by line delivery and pause length rather than editing. The core mechanism is a bait-and-switch reframe: a vulnerable romantic question ('Why don't we do that anymore?') gets answered with genuine-sounding logic that substitutes tolerance of annoying habits for affection, delivered completely deadpan by a visually 'low-battery' (drooping, half-asleep) character design. The longest pause in the clip (0.909s) is saved for right before the closing dismissal, functioning as the joke's timing beat rather than any vocal punch or musical sting.
